A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonstoichiometry and nanoscale inhomogeneity are the most important features of Eu-123 superconductors.
the EuBa2Cu4O6 + δ samples are nonstoichiometric in composition and are inhomogeneous both in composition and structure.

the nanoscale inhomogeneities in the Eu-123 samples can be considered as the main reason of the nonuniform distribution of the superconducting phase and, consequently, of the superconductivity of the Eu-123 oxide samples.

the nanoinhomogeneity in EuBa2Cu 3O6 +δ (Eu-123), which has been found by us, is a general feature of high-temperature cuprate superconductors.
